raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What

`wo_b` in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is a `RowParallelLinear`: an mxfp8 GEMM followed
by an all-reduce of the `[M, hidden]` result. The two can overlap.
`mori.ops.gemm_ar`'s fused kernel writes each destination's row band straight
into a symmetric window and hands it to the SDMA copy engines as soon as that
band's tiles are done, so the transfer runs *inside* the GEMM instead of after
it. The reduce and all-gather still run as their own kernels.

**Opt-in and ROCm gfx950 only.** `fused_wo_b()` returns `None` for everything it
does not serve — decode, small or ragged `M`, a layer neither mxfp8 route
prepared, no SDMA queues — and disables itself for the process on any failure,
so the ordinary path is the fallback rather than an error.

Supersedes #40757, which could not be reopened after its branch was
force-pushed. Same branch, rebased onto current `main`; the first commit is that
PR's content and the second takes it to V4.1-Flash.

## Two switches, and they are not interchangeable

| | TTFT, TP2 | TTFT, TP4 | numerics |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR=1` | **−2.4%** | **−2.0%** | relL2 **7.5e-3 – 8.2e-3** |
| ` + ..._FP8_GATHER=1` | **−5.8%** | **−7.0%** | relL2 **1.87e-2** |

The fp8 gather sends the all-gather leg as e4m3 with a per-row scale. It is
worth more than the fusing itself — and it is the half that costs accuracy, so
it stays off by default.

2x and 4x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 16384 in / 64 out, concurrency 1, the
MI355X cookbook's flags unchanged (including `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter`).
Medians over six fresh server instances per arm, arms interleaved. 48 instances,
24 pairs, every pair agreeing in sign.

### Numerics, measured where the path engages

`SGLANG_DEBUG_FUSED_WO_B_AR=1` reports two things per fused call: the op against
the unfused path, and the op against *itself* on the same inputs immediately
again. 42 samples per arm at M=16384:

**Corrected after review** (thanks @hubertlu-tw). This section claimed the bf16
wire was bit-identical on the cookbook flags. It is not, and the claim was the
wrong half of a real distinction: exactness needs `wo_a` to hand `wo_b` an
`Fp8GridActivation`, which `wo_b_takes_fp8_grid()` only returns for the gfx950
*native* mxfp8 route. The MI355X recipes pin `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter`, where
`wo_b` receives a plain bf16 tensor and the fused and unfused paths each
quantise it themselves.

Re-measured at M=16384, 4x MI355X, TP4, cookbook flags otherwise unchanged:

| | vs unfused | vs itself |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 wire, `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter` | 7.48e-3 .. 8.20e-3 | 0 |
| bf16 wire, `--fp8-gemm-backend auto` | 7.48e-3 .. 7.56e-3 | 0 |
| fp8 wire | 1.844e-2 .. 1.899e-2 | 0 |

The earlier **0** could not be reproduced on either backend value, and the
native route it would require is not one these flags select, so treat it as
withdrawn rather than conditional. The second column staying zero is the part
that holds: the collective is deterministic, without which "lossy but
deterministic" and "non-deterministic" would look the same.

The fp8 wire's spread is 3% of its own value, which is what a fixed mantissa
width looks like rather than a numerical hazard. **What it does to downstream
quality is not measured here**: GSM8K cannot answer it — its 5-shot prompts give
a padded M of ~512 against a floor of 8192, so every arm runs the same code, and
two passes of that same code scored 0.906 and 0.898, which puts its resolution
above 1% anyway.

## Worth a reviewer's attention

* **Both gfx950 mxfp8 routes are served, and the weight's shape cannot say which
  one ran.** The native route rebinds the weight to a shuffled
  `[N/16, K/128, 2048]`; the aiter route — which `--fp8-gemm-backend aiter`
  takes, and which the MI355X cookbook pins — leaves the checkpoint's `[N, K]`.
  `mxfp8_aiter_ready` records it, because reading one layout as the other
  returns an uncorrelated result rather than failing. mori's own `preshuffle_b`
  is defined on exactly what the aiter route leaves, so only the B conversion
  branches.

* **The operand the gfx950 `wo_a` fork emits decides whether this can serve the
  call at all.** An `Fp8GridActivation` unwraps to the bf16 underneath, but an
  `Mxfp8Activation` is already quantised with no bf16 left and the op does its
  own quantisation, so that form keeps the ordinary path. Only decode produces
  it, which the M floor declines anyway.

* **The window is VMM memory outside torch's allocator**, sized from
  `get_schedule().chunked_prefill_size` and unable to grow afterwards (560-640
  MiB at these shapes), so a run that enables this wants a correspondingly lower
  `--mem-fraction-static`. It is taken from the chunked-prefill limit rather
  than the first request seen, so a short prompt arriving first cannot leave a
  window too small for a later full chunk.

* **The thresholds are on the SGLang side on purpose.** `_MIN_FUSED_M` (8192 on
  the bf16 wire, 2048 on the fp8 one) answers "is fusing *worth* it against
  what the model runs today", which is not a property of the kernel;
  `mori.ops.gemm_ar.supports()` answers the separate question of whether the
  shape is expressible.

* **The MORI pin moves to `066fd10e`** so that `export BUILD_CCO_SDMA=ON` can
  come out of the Dockerfile and the CI install script: ROCm/mori#710 made the
  cco SDMA path the default and normalised `1`/`TRUE`/`yes`, which previously
  built a host library with SDMA and JITted a device wrapper without it. The
  guard in `_FusedWoB` stays — a build can still opt out, and the failure mode
  it catches is a collective that moves no bytes and therefore measures
  *faster*.

## How these were measured, because a single pair does not resolve them

Instance-to-instance spread on these boxes is the same order as the effect,
while repeats inside one server instance land within ~1%. An earlier three-pair
run of the same comparison came out at −0.1% with two of its three pairs landing
on the baseline; six pairs of fresh instances put it at −5.8% with all six
agreeing. So: interleave the arms, take the median across instances, keep both
arms in one lease on one node, and record a signal that each arm is what it
claims to be (`window` present, `declines` zero) rather than trusting the switch.

Per-layer timings are deliberately **not** quoted. That harness synchronises
every call, so the transfer sits on the critical path with no neighbouring work
to hide behind — it cannot show an overlap benefit by construction, and its
baseline is the native route rather than the aiter one the server takes. On a
contended node it also inflates the NCCL baseline ~48% while leaving the SDMA
path untouched, which flips the sign.

## Not in this PR

* **The standalone mxfp8 GEMM.** mori's GEMM without a collective attached is
  ~25-30% faster than aiter's at these shapes and serves layers this has nothing
  to fuse with, but it belongs in aiter rather than behind an SGLang switch, and
  is going there instead.
* **Tests.** The perf harnesses this was derived with are not included.
* **V4-Pro.** #40757 measured V4-Pro, whose `wo_b` is a 128x128 block-scale
  linear preshuffled by the aiter block-fp8 route. V4.1-Flash quantises at
  32-wide ue8m0 and takes a gfx950 mxfp8 route, so the second commit replaces
  that path rather than adding to it — those numbers describe the first commit,
  not this PR's head.

nodes.body:
Thanks — all eight were real, and two of them were wrong in ways I had documented in a comment and then not enforced. Fixed in 3dd6ca33 and 18dd7fd4, verified on an 8×MI355X node.

### 1. DP attention: wrong reduction group, possible hang

You're right on both counts, and the second one follows from the first. The gate was on `defer_all_reduce`, which is a different question — everything that made *that* false reached the fused path, including `attn_tp_size == 1` and `1 < attn_tp_size < tp_size`. The env var's comment said "TP-only" and nothing enforced it.

Rather than gate at the call site I put it in `fused_wo_b`, as `_reduces_over_tp_group(layer)`, using `RowParallelLinear.forward`'s own conditions read off the layer — `reduce_results and tp_size > 1`, not `use_decode_attn_tp`, not `use_dp_attention_reduce`, and `tuple(layer.tp_group.ranks) == tuple(get_tp_group().ranks)`. The call site is where this went wrong once; restating the rule there would leave two places to keep in agreement. `should_skip_mlp_all_reduce()` is in the per-forward half of it, which you'll also recognise as a case the old code let through: it made `defer_all_reduce` false, so the fused path performed a reduce the split path would have skipped.

Not gated: `quantize_communications`, which would make the split path's reduce numerically different — `validation_hook.py:263` rejects it on anything but NPU.

Verified end to end: TP2 with `--attn-dp-size 2` (so `attn_tp_size == 1`), switch on, an 8401-token prompt that is eligible on the TP-only run. **Zero** `mori fused wo_b` lines — it declines before constructing anything — and the model answers correctly. Plus a unit check of all six group configurations.

That also closes the hang, since eligibility can only diverge across ranks under DP attention, which no longer reaches `_eligible`.

### 2. A rank-local disable deadlocks the TP group

Agreed, and the architecture was wrong rather than the handler. Construction is now collective: `_construct_collectively` attempts it on every rank, agrees the outcome over `tp.cpu_group`, and the ranks that *succeeded* tear their communicator down when a peer did not — otherwise they hold the window's reservation for a path nothing can use.

After construction there is no fallback left. An OOM in `pad_rows`/`quantize_packed` is rank-local and `run` is collective, so returning None from either is exactly the silent hang you describe; dying is visible. Every remaining reason to decline is an explicit check above that point, and each reads the same on all ranks.

Verified with fault injection under torchrun, both `--fail-rank 0` and `--fail-rank 1`:

```
rank 0: constructed=False  disabled=True  state_kept=False  torn_down=True
rank 1: constructed=False  disabled=True  state_kept=False  torn_down=False
all ranks agree: True
```

### 3. Construction `ValueError` retried every call

Same root cause — one `try` over both construction and the per-call work, with a handler written for the latter. Construction is attempted once and a failure is permanent (and collective).

### 4. Lazy second copy of each `wo_b` weight

`prepare_wo_b_weight` now runs at load time. Worth noting that my first attempt at this **didn't work and the measurement caught it**: I hooked `post_load_weights`, which `loader.py:856` runs *before* `process_weights_after_loading`, so `mxfp8_ready` was false and it returned without allocating — KV cache and available memory came out byte-identical to the switch-off run. It is now in `precompile_kernels_after_loading`, which runs after the layout exists and before the pool is sized.

TP2, identical args, `max_total_num_tokens`:

| | tokens |
|---|---:|
| switch off | 34,249,728 |
| switch on | 33,768,960 |

−480,768 tokens. With four MLA KV source layers that is roughly 1.1 GB, against 40 × 21 MiB ≈ 840 MiB of extra weight — the right order, and the point is that the profiler now sees it at all.

### 5. Window sizing without chunked prefill

Switched to `max_prefill_buffer_tokens()` with `max_prefill_tokens` as the fallback, which is what the other buffer-sizing callers here use and also covers PP dynamic chunking's 1.25× probe. Added the one-line warning when a call exceeds the window.

Verified with `--chunked-prefill-size -1 --max-prefill-tokens 20480`, first eligible request M=8401:

```
mori fused wo_b: window 700 MiB, tp=2, M<=20480, N=5120, K=4096, gather=bf16
```

Sized from the ceiling, not from that first request — which under the old code would have pinned it at ~8448 and declined everything larger for the life of the process.

### 6. Raw `os.environ`

Both go through the `EnvField` API now, and `os` is no longer imported. Your sub-point was the sharper half: `SHAPE_LOG=true` was silently ignored and `override()` did nothing, since it was compared against `"1"` at import time. Checked both in the unit test.

### 7. Duplicated ue8m0 scale rule

The quantiser calls `fp8_grid_quant` and keeps only the packed store. You're right that they are not the same function — `fp8_grid_quant` takes the exponent off the IEEE bits and is exact at powers of two, where `ceil(tl.log2(.))` can land above the integer and pick one exponent higher.

Verified rather than reasoned: operands with whole groups placed on exact powers of two of 448, comparing against `fp8_grid_quantize`. Exponents and fp8 codes are now byte-identical; 0 differing groups.

### 8. Hot-path overhead

The switch is memoised (`_disabled` stays dynamic and is checked first, so the off path is one bool), and `m_pad` is computed once per call instead of three times. I left the call-site caching alone — it's a model-file change for what is now a memoised read.

---

Also re-ran the TP-only path end to end after all of this: fusion still engages at TP2 (`window 560 MiB, M<=16384`), both ranks agree, generation is correct.

All five fixed in `bde0b40a`. You were right about the fault injection — details below.

### 1. Collective construction around `self_test()`

Correct, and the fix needed to go further than I first wrote it.

**Where the fault was injected:** nowhere near that window. I replaced `_FusedWoB` wholesale with a stub, so neither rank did any device work at all; the healthy rank's `torn_down=True` was the stub's `close()`, not a completed `self_test()`. The test exercised the agreement logic and nothing else, which is what its docstring claimed but not what the review needed. Rewritten to build the real communicator and the real op and fail one rank at a chosen point.

Construction now agrees after **each stage that can fail locally**, because the stage after it is collective:

1. build the communicator and the op → agree
2. compile (`warmup()`, which calls mori's `_compiled`) → agree
3. run the device phases (`self_test()`) → agree on the result

Both failure modes you named land in a window that agrees. On 2×MI355X with real mori:

| injected at | result |
|---|---|
| nothing (control) | both ranks construct, no hang |
| inside `GemmAllReduceOp` construction, after `register_window` | both ranks `disabled=True`, **no hang** |
| inside the compile stage | both ranks `disabled=True`, **no hang** |

Stage 2 exists because of your FlyDSL point: `self_test` compiles and *then* launches, so without a split a compile failure on one rank still left its peers in the barrier. Reaching for `op._compiled` is mori-private and I said so at the call site; the public surface has no compile-only entry point.

**What this still cannot cover**, and I verified it rather than assuming: a failure *inside* the device phases, once peers are already in the barrier, still hangs — I injected one and the run sat until I killed it. No host-side agreement around a collective can fix that. Both modes you named happen before that point, so the stages are cut where they can help; past it a watchdog is the only recourse.

Also fixed the `get_unique_id()` ordering: rank 0 now broadcasts a `None` payload on failure instead of going on to the agreement while its peers sit in `broadcast_object_list` on the same group.

### 2. Stale `_mori_b` after a weight update

Confirmed and fixed. `end_weight_update` calls `post_load_weights` only when asked and `precompile_kernels_after_loading` not at all, so no hook-based invalidation is reliable. The cache is now keyed on the source weight's `(id, _version)` for both the weight and its scale — `id` catches a replaced tensor, `_version` an in-place write.

Exercised both shapes an update takes, on device:

```
ok  unchanged weight hits the cache
ok  in-place weight update invalidates      <- same object, same data_ptr
ok  replaced weight invalidates
ok  scale update invalidates
ok  post-update value equals a fresh build
```

The in-place case is the one a key on `data_ptr` alone would have missed.

### 3. Window at load time

Done — `prepare_fused_wo_b` now builds the weight copies *and* the window, and the collective construction runs there rather than inside a forward.

Ordering, from a TP2 startup log:

```
05:02:44 TP0/TP1  mori fused wo_b: window 560 MiB, tp=2, M<=16384, ...
05:04:47 TP0      max_total_num_tokens=33338624, available_gpu_mem=54.85 GB
```

Two minutes before the profiler, and on both ranks. Previously that line appeared during serving, after the KV cache had been sized.

With everything else equal, `max_total_num_tokens` goes 33,706,240 (switch off) → 33,338,624 (on), so the profiler does account for the preparation. I can't cleanly split that number between the weights and the window — `available_gpu_mem` reads 54.84 vs 54.85 GB, so the VMM reservation may not show up there at all — and I'd rather report the ordering, which is unambiguous, than attribute the delta.

The per-call path keeps a construction fallback for a caller that never prepared, and now warns once that it is allocating outside the profiler's budget.

### 4. Scope and release

`prepare_fused_wo_b` takes the layers explicitly: `[m.wo_b for m in self.modules() if isinstance(m, MQALayer)]`. DSPARK's attention has a `wo_b` and calls it directly, and the draft wrapper borrows the method, so the old walk over every module with the attribute prepared copies nothing reads. (That walk was itself a fix for the draft wrapper having no `.model` — it solved that and over-reached.)

Added `_can_ever_fuse`, which also declines a shape `supports()` rejects and an M floor the deployment's prefill ceiling cannot reach — `_eligible`'s floor is monotonic in M, so failing at the ceiling means failing everywhere. A collective disable releases every copy.

Your decode-instance example is only partly covered: an instance that declares a large prefill ceiling but never prefills still pays for the window. Narrowing that needs a signal this layer does not have, and I left it stated rather than guessed at.

### 5. Docstring

It fails at startup, and now says so — the "best effort" paragraph is gone rather than a `try` added. Dropped the redundant `hasattr`.

Both confirmed, and the first one means my previous round's fix did not work. `8925b982`.

### 1. The version-counter key was blind to the write the loaders make

You're right, and the test passing made it worse than not having tried. Measured on torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2:

| write | `_version` | `data_ptr` | storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| `p.data.copy_()` | 0 → 0 | same | same |
| `p.data.add_()` | 0 → 0 | same | same |
| `p.copy_()` | 0 → **1** | same | same |
| `p.view(-1).add_()` | 0 → **1** | same | same |

`linear.py` writes through `.data` in all six weight loaders. And my test used `layer.weight.view(torch.uint8).add_(7)` — the last row — so it exercised a mutation shape the real path never takes. Your guess about what it wrote was right.

Nothing on the tensor moves, so the cache cannot be made to notice. **The update has to be refused**, which is what sglang already has a mechanism for and I should have found before inventing a key: `_unsupported_derived_weight_cache_error` walks the modules for `_derived_weight_cache_error`, and all four update paths check it before writing. Its docstring describes this exact case — "derived weight splits that in-place loader writes do not refresh" — and requires the constraint be startup-determined and rank-uniform, which `_can_ever_fuse` is.

So building a fused copy now publishes it and releasing clears it. The `(id, _version)` key is gone rather than kept as a second line of defence, since a key that cannot work is worse than none.

Verified against the updater's own function rather than by reading:

```
ok  clean model allows updates
ok  a fused copy blocks updates
ok  the reason says what to turn off
ok  the cache is indeed blind to a .data write   <- the premise, asserted
ok  releasing lifts the constraint
ok  a rebuild after release sees the new weight
```

The fourth line is deliberate: it asserts the failure mode still exists, so if a future torch makes `.data` writes observable the test says so instead of silently protecting nothing.

Your `id`-reuse point is moot now — there is no key — but it was correct.

### 2. The NextN draft built a second communicator and window

Confirmed: `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMNextN` overrides only `load_weights` and `post_load_weights`, its model builds a `DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` (`deepseek_v4_nextn.py:97`), and `_build_self_attn` returns an `MQALayer`. So with MTP this ran a second time in the same process and `_construct_collectively` ended with an unconditional `_state = state`.

`prepare_fused_wo_b` now reuses an existing op when `(n, k)` match and `m_max` fits, and declines otherwise with a log line — `fused_wo_b` would reject those layers against `_state` anyway, so preparing them would allocate copies nothing reads.

On the second point you raised there: prepared layers are tracked across models and `_disable` releases all of them. Previously a second model's failure turned the path off for the first model's layers while leaving their copies allocated.

### Regression

TP2 dummy-weight startup is unchanged: window built at 11:09:43, profiler at 11:11:43, `max_total_num_tokens=33338624` — identical to the previous round — and no tracebacks.

### What this costs

A server running with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR=1` can no longer take online weight updates; it gets a clear error naming the switch to turn off. That is a real restriction, and it is the one the mHC splits and the HPC-Ops bf16xfp32 GEMM already accept for the same reason. If the RL flow matters more than the fusion for a given deployment, the switch is the answer; if you'd rather I made the copies refreshable instead, that needs a hook in the update paths that does not exist today, and I'd rather add it as its own change than fold it in here.

@hubertlu-tw Added in `ec04a599e0`. Three files, split by what each one needs to run:

**`test/registered/amd/test_mori_gemm_ar.py`** — mori stubbed, so it runs on any gfx950 image. Covers `_reduces_over_tp_group` (the attn-DP / decode-attn-TP / subgroup cases where fusing would reduce over the wrong ranks), `_eligible`'s two wire floors and the pad-fill bound, and the weight-update refusal. Registered to `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`, 4s.

**`test/registered/amd/test_mori_gemm_ar_contract.py`** — the interface guard you asked for. Every mori symbol the adapter calls is bound with the exact arguments it passes:

```
padded_m, supports, preshuffle_b, preshuffle_a_scale,
Communicator.init / .get_unique_id, UniqueId.from_bytes,
GemmAllReduceOp.window_bytes_for / __init__ / _compiled / self_test / pad_rows / __call__
```

plus the two operand conversions this module writes itself, against mori's own helpers: `quantize_packed`'s packed A-scale equals `preshuffle_a_scale` of the canonical quantiser's exponents (value for value, which also pins that the two scale rules agree), and `mori_weight`'s output equals `preshuffle_b` on both the native and the aiter route. Same suite, 4s.

**`test/registered/amd/test_mori_gemm_ar_collective.py`** — spawns the TP group. A failure on exactly one rank at each of the three construction stages must disable the path on every rank and release what the successful ones built; a rank that cannot produce the unique id must not strand its peers in the broadcast; and the fused result must match the split path to 2e-2 relative L2. Registered to `stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x`, 84s at TP8 on MI355X.

**CI registration.** Besides the suites above, there is a new `mori-gemm-ar` job in `pr-test-amd-mori.yml` that runs all three where mori is guaranteed present. Unlike `mori-pd` / `mori-hicache` it is deliberately **not** label-only — a change to `mori_gemm_ar.py` or to the pinned `MORI_COMMIT` in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` triggers it, since a mori whose `gemm_ar` signatures moved is exactly the breakage you are asking to guard against, and a PR bumping that commit would otherwise never run the test that catches it.

Two things worth flagging from writing these:

1. The job sets `MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`. Without it the cco puts compile to nothing — the first TP8 run here failed on `self_test` with `the all-reduce returned 0 where 36 was expected`, which is the exact silent-wrong-answer case `self_test` exists for, hit on a real environment on the first try.
2. Every case was checked against a mutation of the behaviour it guards (dropping the tp-group ranks comparison, collapsing the two wire floors, breaking the packed-scale permutation, skipping `state.close()` in `_disable`, removing one stage's agreement, removing the broadcast-before-raise). All ten go red.

I also verified the adapter binds cleanly against the currently pinned `MORI_COMMIT=f39fa765` — every symbol exists with a matching signature there, so the contract test is green today rather than reporting an existing break.

Thanks @yangyuhuiling for adding the tests to SGLang.

I have a few concerns as follows. Please feel free to correct me if I missed anything from my local tests.

## Review: test results on 8x MI355X

I tested head `a8b0165` with mori `f39fa765`, which is the pin in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` on main and is built with `BUILD_CCO_SDMA=ON`. The PR and mori were both run unmodified. The host is 8x MI355X (gfx950) with amdgpu 6.16.13 on Linux 5.15. All GPUs are connected over XGMI.

I used the two sgl-dev nightly images, both of which ship mori `f39fa765` with `BUILD_CCO_SDMA=ON`:

| Image | ROCm | torch / HIP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm10-mi35x-20261014` | 10.0.0 (pip SDK) | `2.11.0+rocm10.0.0` / 7.15.26333 |
| `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261014` | 7.2.4 | `2.11.0+rocm7.2` / 7.2.26015 |

Both images have FlyDSL 0.3.4.1.

### Summary

On this host I could not get the expected behavior from either image:

| Image | SDMA | mori `gemm-only` (TP4, M=16384, N=5120, K=2048) | PR behavior |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `rocm10` | puts move no data | 178.9 µs (mori README: 180.2 µs) | server hangs in `self_test()` |
| `rocm724` | works | 3338.4 µs (18.7x slower) | correct, but TTFT is +157% to +204% |

The hardware checks out: torch GEMM, RCCL, and peer copy all give normal numbers (details at the end). The main concerns are when the fused path may replace `wo_b`'s own reduction, and how failures are handled across ranks:

**Should be fixed before merge**
1. DP attention: wrong reduction group, and a possible cross-rank hang (`deepseek_v4.py`)
2. A rank-local disable deadlocks the TP group on mori's device barriers (`mori_gemm_ar.py`)

**Should fix**

3. A construction-time `ValueError` is retried on every call
4. A lazily allocated second copy of each `wo_b` weight, outside the memory profiler

**Smaller**

Details inline.

**DP attention: the fused path all-reduces over the wrong group, and can hang.**

`fused_wo_b` always reduces over `get_tp_group()` (full TP), but `wo_b` is an attn-TP linear. With `--attn-dp-size 8` (the MI355X balanced / high-throughput recipes in the DeepSeek-V4 cookbook), `attn_tp_size == 1`: `defer_all_reduce` is False, the unfused path does no cross-rank reduction, and the fused path sums rows from 8 unrelated DP ranks. With `1 < attn_tp_size < tp_size`, line 2645 then runs `attn_tp_all_reduce` on top of the full-TP sum.

It can also deadlock: under DP attention each rank has its own M, so `_eligible` differs across ranks. mori requires every rank to call the op the same number of times in the same order (its phases carry device-side cross-rank barriers), so one rank entering `Communicator.init` / the op while a peer falls back to the split path never returns.

The env var's comment says "TP-only", but nothing enforces it. Suggest gating the call here, e.g. only when `self.attn_tp_size == get_parallel().tp_size and self.wo_b.reduce_results`.

**A failure on one rank deadlocks the whole TP group.**

`_disabled` is set only on the rank that raised. That rank then falls back to `self.wo_b(...)`, i.e. an NCCL all-reduce, while its peers keep calling the mori op. mori's `drain` / `gather` phases end in device-side cross-rank barriers (`kernels_sdma.build_sdma_phases`), so the peers spin on the GPU waiting for a rank that never arrives: no timeout, no error, just a hung server.

Rank-local failures are realistic here: an OOM in `pad_rows` / `quantize_packed` / `mori_weight` (see the comment on `mori_weight`), or `alloc_mem` failing on one rank inside `_FusedWoB.__init__` while the others have already entered `self_test()`, which is itself a collective.

The enable/disable decision needs to be collective. E.g. agree on the outcome of construction across `tp.cpu_group` (all-gather a success flag) before any rank uses the op, and treat failures after construction as fatal rather than silently falling back on one rank.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Fused GEMM + all-reduce for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ``wo_b`` on ROCm gfx950, via mori cco.
+
+``wo_b`` is a ``RowParallelLinear``: an mxfp8 GEMM and then an all-reduce of the
+``[M, hidden]`` result. mori's fused kernel writes each destination's row band
+into a symmetric window and hands it to the SDMA copy engines as soon as that
+band's tiles are done, so the transfer runs inside the GEMM; the reduce and
+all-gather still run as their own kernels.
+
+A mori built with ``BUILD_CCO_SDMA=OFF`` compiles the puts out, and then the
+all-reduce returns mostly the local slice while the model still answers -- and
+measures *faster*, having moved no bytes. ``GemmAllReduceOp.self_test()`` is
+what catches that; the flag has been ON by default since ROCm/mori#710.
+
+Needs ``MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`` at process start and a layer one of the two gfx950
+mxfp8 routes prepared -- see ``mxfp8_route``.
+
+The fused epilogue pushes a whole ``BLOCK_M`` row band to one destination, so M
+must be a multiple of ``tp_size * 256``. That granule is mxfp8's, not a choice
+-- see ``_BLOCK_M``. Ragged M is zero-padded up to it, which costs GEMM rows and
+buys the overlap -- see ``_MIN_PAD_FILL``. Decode and small batches fall back to
+the ordinary path, and that is expected rather than a failure.
+
+``mori.ops.gemm_ar.GemmAllReduceOp`` owns the symmetric window, the per-M
+compile cache and the row padding. What stays here is sglang's: the TP
+communicator, how the window is sized, the operand conversions, and whether
+fusing is worth it at this shape.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# ---- operand conversion ----------------------------------------------
+
+#: Rows one packed A-scale group spans, and the rows one quantiser program owns.
+#: They are the same 64 by construction, which is what lets the quantiser write
+#: mori's layout without any extra traffic -- see `_mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel`.
+QUANT_BLOCK_M = 64
+
+
+def mxfp8_shape(layer) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """The layer's logical ``(N, K)``, read off the ue8m0 scale.
+
+    **Not** ``layer.weight.shape``: the native route rebinds the weight to its
+    shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, and reading that first axis as N
+    disqualifies every layer without a word.
+    """
+    sn, sk = layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0.shape
+    return sn * 32, sk * 32
+
+
+def mxfp8_route(layer) -> str | None:
+    """Which gfx950 mxfp8 route prepared this layer, or None if neither did.
+
+    Both leave the ``[N/32, K/32]`` exponent bytes on
+    ``layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0`` and differ only in the weight: ``native``
+    rebinds it to the shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, ``aiter`` leaves plain
+    ``[N, K]``. Reading one as the other returns an uncorrelated result rather
+    than failing, so `mori_weight` branches on this instead of guessing.
+    """
+    if not hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_mx_e8m0"):
+        return None
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_native_ready", False):
+        return "native"
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_aiter_ready", False):
+        return "aiter"
+    return None
+
+
+def mxfp8_ready(layer) -> bool:
+    """Whether either gfx950 mxfp8 route already prepared this layer."""
+    return mxfp8_route(layer) is not None
+
+
+def mori_weight(layer):
+    """The layer's B operand and B scale in mori's layouts, cached on the layer.
+
+    sglang and mori differ only in how a lane's two 64-wide K sub-blocks sit:
+    sglang interleaves them inside its 32 bytes, mori keeps them as two 16-byte
+    blocks. Cached because the permutation copies the whole weight.
+    """
+    cached = getattr(layer, "_mori_b", None)
+    if cached is not None:
+        return cached
+    n, k = mxfp8_shape(layer)
+    w = layer.weight.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    if mxfp8_route(layer) == "aiter":
+        # That route leaves the weight in its checkpoint [N, K] order, which is
+        # what preshuffle_b is defined on, so mori emits its own layout from the
+        # source rather than permuting sglang's.
+        from mori.ops.gemm_ar import preshuffle_b
+
+        b = preshuffle_b(w.reshape(n, k).view(layer.weight.dtype))
+    else:
+        # [N/16, K/128, 64 lanes, 2 sub-blocks, 16B] -> the two sub-blocks split out
+        b = (
+            w.reshape(n // 16, k // 128, 64, 2, 16)
+            .permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+            .contiguous()
+            .reshape(n, k)
+            .view(layer.weight.dtype)
+        )

+        .view(torch.uint8)

+        .to(torch.int32)
+        .reshape(-1)

+
+    Free here: the destination stays inside the 64 bytes this program already
+    owns, so only the store's order changes.
+    """
+    pid_m = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_b = tl.program_id(1)
+    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    offs_k = pid_b * 32 + tl.arange(0, 32)
+    m_mask = offs_m < M
+    x = tl.load(
+        x_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * sxm + offs_k[None, :] * sxk,
+        mask=m_mask[:, None],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    amax = tl.maximum(tl.max(tl.abs(x), axis=1), 1e-30)
+    sb = tl.ceil(tl.log2(amax / 448.0)) + 127.0
+    sb = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(sb, 0.0), 254.0)
+    descale = tl.exp2(sb - 127.0)
+    xq = tl.clamp(x / descale[:, None], -448.0, 448.0).to(xq_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+    tl.store(
+        xq_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * sqm + offs_k[None, :] * sqk,
+        xq,
+        mask=m_mask[:, None],
+    )
+    dst = pid_b * M + (offs_m // 64) * 64 + (offs_m % 16) * 4 + (offs_m % 64) // 16
+    tl.store(s_ptr + dst, sb.to(tl.uint8), mask=m_mask)
+
+
+def quantize_packed(x: torch.Tensor):
+    """bf16 ``[M, K]`` -> (fp8 e4m3 values, mori's packed ue8m0 A scale).
+
+    ``M`` must be a multiple of `QUANT_BLOCK_M`; pad the bf16 input first, so
+    the scale is built over the padded M and its packed layout needs no repair.
+    """
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import MXFP8_VALUE_DTYPE
+
+    m, k = x.shape
+    xq = torch.empty((m, k), dtype=MXFP8_VALUE_DTYPE, device=x.device)
+    scale = torch.empty((k // 32) * m, dtype=torch.uint8, device=x.device)
+    _mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel[(triton.cdiv(m, QUANT_BLOCK_M), k // 32)](
+        x,
+        xq,
+        scale,
+        m,
+        k,
+        x.stride(0),
+        x.stride(1),
+        xq.stride(0),
+        xq.stride(1),
+        BLOCK_M=QUANT_BLOCK_M,
+    )
+    return xq, scale.view(torch.int32)
+
+
+#: Smallest padded M worth fusing on a **bf16** wire, measured against what
+#: V4.1-Flash runs today. 5120 is not one answer: the fused cost is fixed by the
+#: padded size while the baseline follows the true M, so what separates the
+#: winning shapes from the losing ones is a floor rather than a fill ratio.
+_MIN_FUSED_M = 8192
+#: The same for the **fp8** wire, a lower bar because that wire runs 15-25%
+#: under the bf16 one. Only m_pad 1024 loses: one row band per destination
+#: leaves the scatter nothing to overlap with.
+_MIN_FUSED_M_FP8_GATHER = 2048
+#: Padding buys the overlap and costs GEMM rows, so a ragged M has to be full
+#: enough that the gain at the padded size still clears it. Binds on the fp8
+#: wire only: at m_pad >= 8192 the granule already puts the worst fill at 0.875.
+_MIN_PAD_FILL = 0.80
+_state: _FusedWoB | None = None
+_disabled = False
+_warned_layout = False
+_warned_reject = False
+_mori_ok: bool | None = None
+
+#: M is the token count of one forward, not of one request, so whether the
+#: fused path engages depends on how the scheduler batches it.
+_SHAPE_LOG = os.environ.get("SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_SHAPE_LOG") == "1"
+_shape_hist: dict = {}
+_shape_calls = 0
+#: 61 wo_b calls make one forward, so this logs roughly every ten of them.
+_SHAPE_EVERY = 610
+
+
+def _record_shape(m, eligible, world_size):
+    global _shape_calls
+    key = (m, _padded_m(m, world_size), bool(eligible))
+    _shape_hist[key] = _shape_hist.get(key, 0) + 1
+    _shape_calls += 1
+    if _shape_calls >= _SHAPE_EVERY:
+        _shape_calls = 0
+        items = sorted(_shape_hist.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
+        logger.info(
+            "wo_b shapes: %s",
+            " ".join(f"M={m}/pad{p}{'+' if e else '-'}x{c}" for (m, p, e), c in items),
+        )
+        _shape_hist.clear()
+
+
+#: mori's mxfp8 kernel packs a lane's four M tiles into one scale dword and
+#: picks the byte with the MFMA's opsel, which is four tiles only at BLOCK_M 256
+#: -- so a destination's row band is 256 rows here, not blockscale's 128, and M
+#: pads to a multiple of ``tp_size * 256``.
+_BLOCK_M = 256
+
+
+def _padded_m(m: int, world_size: int) -> int:
+    from mori.ops.gemm_ar import padded_m
+
+    return padded_m(m, world_size, _BLOCK_M)
+
+
+_logged_config = False
+
+
+def _shuffled_once():
+    global _logged_config
+    if _logged_config:
+        return True
+    _logged_config = True
+    return False
+
+
+def _fused_weight(layer):
+    """The op's B operand and B scale, or None if this layer cannot be fused."""
+    global _warned_layout
+    if not mxfp8_ready(layer):
+        if not _warned_layout:
+            _warned_layout = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "mori fused wo_b: neither gfx950 mxfp8 route prepared this "
+                "layer (weight shape %s), which the fused kernel requires; "
+                "not fusing.",
+                tuple(layer.weight.shape),
+            )
+        return None
+    return mori_weight(layer)
+
+
+class _FusedWoB:
+    """The TP communicator and mori's op, one per rank.
+
+    Holds the cco ``Communicator`` built from sglang's TP group, which is the
+    part mori cannot construct for us.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, m_max: int, n: int, k: int):
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+        from mori.cco import Communicator, UniqueId
+        from mori.ops.gemm_ar import GemmAllReduceOp
+        from sglang.srt.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+        tp = get_tp_group()
+        self.rank = tp.rank_in_group
+        self.world_size = tp.world_size
+        self.n, self.k, self.m_max = n, k, m_max
+
+        payload = [bytes(Communicator.get_unique_id()) if self.rank == 0 else None]
+        dist.broadcast_object_list(payload, src=tp.ranks[0], group=tp.cpu_group)
+        uid = UniqueId.from_bytes(payload[0])
+
+        # The window is VMM memory outside torch's allocator, so the run has to
+        # leave room for it (lower --mem-fraction-static). Sized from m_max, and
+        # it cannot grow afterwards.
+        gather_dtype = (
+            "fp8" if envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_FP8_GATHER.get() else "bf16"
+        )
+        window_bytes = GemmAllReduceOp.window_bytes_for(
+            self.world_size,
+            m_max=m_max,
+            n=n,
+            block_m=_BLOCK_M,
+            gather_dtype=gather_dtype,
+        )
+        self._comm_ctx = Communicator.init(
+            self.world_size,
+            self.rank,
+            uid,
+            per_rank_vmm=4 * window_bytes + (512 << 20),
+        )
+        self.comm = self._comm_ctx.__enter__()
+        try:
+            # Which way the fp8 gather moves. The LSA pull widens on the way in
+            # instead of in a second kernel, and it wins in both places: 951us
+            # against SDMA's 1011 on the layer, 1041.2ms of GPU busy against
+            # 1052.1 in the server.
+            self.op = GemmAllReduceOp(
+                self.comm,
+                n=n,
+                k=k,
+                m_max=m_max,
+                quant="mxfp8",
+                gather_dtype=gather_dtype,
+                gather_transport=os.environ.get(
+                    "SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_GATHER_TRANSPORT", "lsa"
+                ),
+            )
+            # Prove the collective moves bytes before serving a token. A mori
+            # built with BUILD_CCO_SDMA=OFF compiles the puts out: the kernels
+            # still launch, the all-reduce returns mostly the local slice, and
+            # the model answers fluently while being wrong -- and measures
+            # *faster*, having moved nothing.
+            self.op.self_test()
+        except Exception:
+            # The communicator holds a VMM reservation the whole process pays
+            # for. Half-constructing this object and leaving it open makes the
+            # *fallback* path fail too, which is how a simple attribute error
+            # here once took the server down.
+            self._comm_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
+            raise
+        logger.info(
+            "mori fused wo_b: window %.0f MiB, tp=%d, M<=%d, N=%d, K=%d, gather=%s",
+            self.op.window_bytes / 2**20,
+            self.world_size,
+            m_max,
+            n,
+            k,
+            gather_dtype,
+        )
+
+    def pad_rows(self, x: torch.Tensor, m_pad: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.op.pad_rows(x, m_pad)
+
+    def run(self, q_input, x_scale_raw, weight, weight_scale) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.op(q_input, weight, x_scale_raw, weight_scale)
+
+
+def _window_m_max(m_pad: int, world_size: int) -> int:
+    """Rows the symmetric window is sized for.
+
+    Taken from the chunked-prefill limit rather than the first request seen, so
+    a short prompt arriving first cannot fix a window too small for a full chunk
+    later -- the window cannot grow once allocated.
+    """
+    # `get_global_server_args()` is retired; the scheduling namespace carries
+    # the value in effect, which is what the other layers read.
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_schedule
+
+    limit = get_schedule().chunked_prefill_size
+    if limit is not None and limit > 0:
+        return max(m_pad, _padded_m(limit, world_size))
+    return m_pad
+
+
+def _eligible(m: int, n: int, k: int, world_size: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether fusing is both expressible and worth it at this shape.
+
+    mori's ``supports`` answers the first; the thresholds here answer the
+    second, which is not a property of the kernel.
+    """
+    from mori.ops.gemm_ar import supports
+
+    if not supports(m, n, k, world_size, quant="mxfp8"):
+        return False
+    floor = (
+        _MIN_FUSED_M_FP8_GATHER
+        if envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_FP8_GATHER.get()
+        else _MIN_FUSED_M
+    )
+    m_pad = _padded_m(m, world_size)
+    return m_pad >= floor and m >= _MIN_PAD_FILL * m_pad
+
+
+def _mori_has_gemm_ar() -> bool:
+    """Whether the pinned mori carries ``ops.gemm_ar``, memoised.
+
+    Checked rather than assumed because the import sits on the per-call path
+    below the switch: a mori predating the op would raise from inside a forward
+    rather than fall back.
+    """
+    global _mori_ok, _disabled
+    if _mori_ok is None:
+        try:
+            import mori.ops.gemm_ar  # noqa: F401
+
+            _mori_ok = True
+        except ImportError as err:
+            _mori_ok = False
+            _disabled = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "mori fused wo_b: this mori has no ops.gemm_ar, so the fused "
+                "path is off for this process: %s",
+                err,
+            )
+    return _mori_ok
+
+
+def fused_wo_b_available() -> bool:
+    """Static gate, cheap enough to call per layer."""
+    return (
+        not _disabled
+        and envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR.get()
+        and _mori_has_gemm_ar()
+    )
+
+
+def fused_wo_b(layer, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """wo_b's `GEMM + all-reduce`, fused. ``None`` means "use the normal path".
+
+    ``x`` is the bf16 activation this rank holds, ``[M, K]``. The result is the
+    all-reduced ``[M, N]``, as a **view of the symmetric window** -- the next
+    layer's wo_b overwrites it, which is safe because the caller consumes it in
+    the residual add of the same layer. ``SGLANG_DEBUG_FUSED_WO_B_AR`` forces a copy
+    and cross-checks against the unfused path.
+    """
+    global _state, _disabled
+
+    if not fused_wo_b_available():
+        return None
+
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import Fp8GridActivation
+    from sglang.srt.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    # wo_a hands wo_b either a plain bf16 activation or an Fp8GridActivation --
+    # a bf16 tensor already rounded onto wo_b's fp8 grid, so quantising it below
+    # is lossless rather than a second rounding. Either way what the GEMM needs
+    # is the bf16 tensor.
+    if isinstance(x, Fp8GridActivation):
+        x = x.x
+    # wo_a's MXFP8 epilogue (SGLANG_HIP_WO_A_MXFP8) instead hands over fp8 plus
+    # a ue8m0 scale, with no bf16 left to quantise, and the op does its own
+    # quantisation. Only decode reaches that form, which _eligible declines on
+    # M anyway, so declining here costs no fusing.
+    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        return None
+
+    m, k = x.shape
+    if not hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_mx_e8m0"):
+        return None
+    n, w_k = mxfp8_shape(layer)
+    if w_k != k:
+        return None
+    world_size = get_tp_group().world_size
+    eligible = _eligible(m, n, k, world_size)
+    if _SHAPE_LOG:
+        _record_shape(m, eligible, world_size)
+    if not eligible:
+        return None
+
+    m_pad = _padded_m(m, world_size)
+    try:
+        if _state is None:
+            _state = _FusedWoB(
+                m_max=_window_m_max(m_pad, world_size),
+                n=n,
+                k=k,
+            )
+        if m_pad > _state.m_max or n != _state.n or k != _state.k:
+            return None
+        prepared = _fused_weight(layer)
+        if prepared is None:
+            return None
+        weight, b_scale = prepared
+        x_in = x if m_pad == m else _state.pad_rows(x, m_pad)
+        # The quantiser writes mori's packed scale layout itself, so there is no
+        # conversion pass after it. Zero-padded rows quantise to zero values
+        # (their scale is tiny but finite), and rows are independent in a GEMM,
+        # so the padding contributes nothing to any real row.
+        q_input, x_scale = quantize_packed(x_in)
+        out = _state.run(q_input, x_scale, weight, b_scale)
+        out = out[:m]
+    except ValueError as err:
+        # A shape or contract rejection is about *this call*, not about the
+        # path. Disabling the process on one would be a standing hazard: the op
+        # raises ValueError for an M it cannot serve, and a server's M changes
+        # with every batch, so one unlucky shape used to switch the whole
+        # optimisation off for good.
+        global _warned_reject
+        if not _warned_reject:
+            _warned_reject = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "mori fused wo_b declined a call and fell back for it; further "
+                "declines are silent: %s",
+                err,
+            )
+        return None
+    except Exception as err:  # noqa: BLE001 - anything else is not per-call

nodes.body:
**A `ValueError` raised while constructing `_FusedWoB` is retried on every call.**

This handler is meant for per-call rejections, but it also catches `ValueError`s from construction: `GemmAllReduceOp.__init__` raises `ValueError` for an invalid `gather_transport` (e.g. `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_GATHER_TRANSPORT=SDMA`), an unsupported shape, etc., after `Communicator.init` has already run. `_state` stays `None`, so every eligible call (61 per forward) repeats `broadcast_object_list` + `Communicator.init` (a `4 * window + 512 MiB` VMM reservation) + teardown, and after the first warning this is silent.

Suggest handling construction failures separately from per-call rejections and disabling permanently on them (collectively, see the comment below).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Fused GEMM + all-reduce for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ``wo_b`` on ROCm gfx950, via mori cco.
+
+``wo_b`` is a ``RowParallelLinear``: an mxfp8 GEMM and then an all-reduce of the
+``[M, hidden]`` result. mori's fused kernel writes each destination's row band
+into a symmetric window and hands it to the SDMA copy engines as soon as that
+band's tiles are done, so the transfer runs inside the GEMM; the reduce and
+all-gather still run as their own kernels.
+
+A mori built with ``BUILD_CCO_SDMA=OFF`` compiles the puts out, and then the
+all-reduce returns mostly the local slice while the model still answers -- and
+measures *faster*, having moved no bytes. ``GemmAllReduceOp.self_test()`` is
+what catches that; the flag has been ON by default since ROCm/mori#710.
+
+Needs ``MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`` at process start and a layer one of the two gfx950
+mxfp8 routes prepared -- see ``mxfp8_route``.
+
+The fused epilogue pushes a whole ``BLOCK_M`` row band to one destination, so M
+must be a multiple of ``tp_size * 256``. That granule is mxfp8's, not a choice
+-- see ``_BLOCK_M``. Ragged M is zero-padded up to it, which costs GEMM rows and
+buys the overlap -- see ``_MIN_PAD_FILL``. Decode and small batches fall back to
+the ordinary path, and that is expected rather than a failure.
+
+``mori.ops.gemm_ar.GemmAllReduceOp`` owns the symmetric window, the per-M
+compile cache and the row padding. What stays here is sglang's: the TP
+communicator, how the window is sized, the operand conversions, and whether
+fusing is worth it at this shape.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# ---- operand conversion ----------------------------------------------
+
+#: Rows one packed A-scale group spans, and the rows one quantiser program owns.
+#: They are the same 64 by construction, which is what lets the quantiser write
+#: mori's layout without any extra traffic -- see `_mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel`.
+QUANT_BLOCK_M = 64
+
+
+def mxfp8_shape(layer) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """The layer's logical ``(N, K)``, read off the ue8m0 scale.
+
+    **Not** ``layer.weight.shape``: the native route rebinds the weight to its
+    shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, and reading that first axis as N
+    disqualifies every layer without a word.
+    """
+    sn, sk = layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0.shape
+    return sn * 32, sk * 32
+
+
+def mxfp8_route(layer) -> str | None:
+    """Which gfx950 mxfp8 route prepared this layer, or None if neither did.
+
+    Both leave the ``[N/32, K/32]`` exponent bytes on
+    ``layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0`` and differ only in the weight: ``native``
+    rebinds it to the shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, ``aiter`` leaves plain
+    ``[N, K]``. Reading one as the other returns an uncorrelated result rather
+    than failing, so `mori_weight` branches on this instead of guessing.
+    """
+    if not hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_mx_e8m0"):
+        return None
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_native_ready", False):
+        return "native"
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_aiter_ready", False):
+        return "aiter"
+    return None
+
+
+def mxfp8_ready(layer) -> bool:
+    """Whether either gfx950 mxfp8 route already prepared this layer."""
+    return mxfp8_route(layer) is not None
+
+
+def mori_weight(layer):
+    """The layer's B operand and B scale in mori's layouts, cached on the layer.
+
+    sglang and mori differ only in how a lane's two 64-wide K sub-blocks sit:
+    sglang interleaves them inside its 32 bytes, mori keeps them as two 16-byte
+    blocks. Cached because the permutation copies the whole weight.
+    """
+    cached = getattr(layer, "_mori_b", None)
+    if cached is not None:
+        return cached
+    n, k = mxfp8_shape(layer)
+    w = layer.weight.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    if mxfp8_route(layer) == "aiter":
+        # That route leaves the weight in its checkpoint [N, K] order, which is
+        # what preshuffle_b is defined on, so mori emits its own layout from the
+        # source rather than permuting sglang's.
+        from mori.ops.gemm_ar import preshuffle_b
+
+        b = preshuffle_b(w.reshape(n, k).view(layer.weight.dtype))
+    else:
+        # [N/16, K/128, 64 lanes, 2 sub-blocks, 16B] -> the two sub-blocks split out
+        b = (
+            w.reshape(n // 16, k // 128, 64, 2, 16)
+            .permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+            .contiguous()
+            .reshape(n, k)
+            .view(layer.weight.dtype)
+        )
+    b_scale = (
+        layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0.data.contiguous()
+        .view(torch.uint8)
+        .t()
+        .contiguous()
+        .to(torch.int32)
+        .reshape(-1)
+    )
+    layer._mori_b = (b, b_scale)
+    return layer._mori_b
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    xq_ptr,
+    s_ptr,
+    M,
+    K,
+    sxm,
+    sxk,
+    sqm,
+    sqk,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """sglang's ``_mxfp8_quant_kernel`` writing mori's scale layout directly.
+
+    A variant rather than a stride argument on the original, because the layout
+    is not expressible as strides: mori wants element ``(m, kb)`` at
+    ``kb*M + (m//64)*64 + (m%16)*4 + (m%64)//16``, which permutes *within* each
+    64-row group so a lane's four M tiles land in one dword.
+
+    Free here: the destination stays inside the 64 bytes this program already
+    owns, so only the store's order changes.
+    """
+    pid_m = tl.program_id(0)
+    pid_b = tl.program_id(1)
+    offs_m = pid_m * BLOCK_M + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    offs_k = pid_b * 32 + tl.arange(0, 32)
+    m_mask = offs_m < M
+    x = tl.load(
+        x_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * sxm + offs_k[None, :] * sxk,
+        mask=m_mask[:, None],
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    amax = tl.maximum(tl.max(tl.abs(x), axis=1), 1e-30)
+    sb = tl.ceil(tl.log2(amax / 448.0)) + 127.0
+    sb = tl.minimum(tl.maximum(sb, 0.0), 254.0)
+    descale = tl.exp2(sb - 127.0)
+    xq = tl.clamp(x / descale[:, None], -448.0, 448.0).to(xq_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+    tl.store(
+        xq_ptr + offs_m[:, None] * sqm + offs_k[None, :] * sqk,
+        xq,
+        mask=m_mask[:, None],
+    )
+    dst = pid_b * M + (offs_m // 64) * 64 + (offs_m % 16) * 4 + (offs_m % 64) // 16
+    tl.store(s_ptr + dst, sb.to(tl.uint8), mask=m_mask)
+
+
+def quantize_packed(x: torch.Tensor):
+    """bf16 ``[M, K]`` -> (fp8 e4m3 values, mori's packed ue8m0 A scale).
+
+    ``M`` must be a multiple of `QUANT_BLOCK_M`; pad the bf16 input first, so
+    the scale is built over the padded M and its packed layout needs no repair.
+    """
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import MXFP8_VALUE_DTYPE
+
+    m, k = x.shape
+    xq = torch.empty((m, k), dtype=MXFP8_VALUE_DTYPE, device=x.device)
+    scale = torch.empty((k // 32) * m, dtype=torch.uint8, device=x.device)
+    _mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel[(triton.cdiv(m, QUANT_BLOCK_M), k // 32)](
+        x,
+        xq,
+        scale,
+        m,
+        k,
+        x.stride(0),
+        x.stride(1),
+        xq.stride(0),
+        xq.stride(1),
+        BLOCK_M=QUANT_BLOCK_M,
+    )
+    return xq, scale.view(torch.int32)
+
+
+#: Smallest padded M worth fusing on a **bf16** wire, measured against what
+#: V4.1-Flash runs today. 5120 is not one answer: the fused cost is fixed by the
+#: padded size while the baseline follows the true M, so what separates the
+#: winning shapes from the losing ones is a floor rather than a fill ratio.
+_MIN_FUSED_M = 8192
+#: The same for the **fp8** wire, a lower bar because that wire runs 15-25%
+#: under the bf16 one. Only m_pad 1024 loses: one row band per destination
+#: leaves the scatter nothing to overlap with.
+_MIN_FUSED_M_FP8_GATHER = 2048
+#: Padding buys the overlap and costs GEMM rows, so a ragged M has to be full
+#: enough that the gain at the padded size still clears it. Binds on the fp8
+#: wire only: at m_pad >= 8192 the granule already puts the worst fill at 0.875.
+_MIN_PAD_FILL = 0.80
+_state: _FusedWoB | None = None
+_disabled = False
+_warned_layout = False
+_warned_reject = False
+_mori_ok: bool | None = None
+
+#: M is the token count of one forward, not of one request, so whether the
+#: fused path engages depends on how the scheduler batches it.
+_SHAPE_LOG = os.environ.get("SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_SHAPE_LOG") == "1"
+_shape_hist: dict = {}
+_shape_calls = 0
+#: 61 wo_b calls make one forward, so this logs roughly every ten of them.
+_SHAPE_EVERY = 610
+
+
+def _record_shape(m, eligible, world_size):
+    global _shape_calls
+    key = (m, _padded_m(m, world_size), bool(eligible))
+    _shape_hist[key] = _shape_hist.get(key, 0) + 1
+    _shape_calls += 1
+    if _shape_calls >= _SHAPE_EVERY:
+        _shape_calls = 0
+        items = sorted(_shape_hist.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
+        logger.info(
+            "wo_b shapes: %s",
+            " ".join(f"M={m}/pad{p}{'+' if e else '-'}x{c}" for (m, p, e), c in items),
+        )
+        _shape_hist.clear()
+
+
+#: mori's mxfp8 kernel packs a lane's four M tiles into one scale dword and
+#: picks the byte with the MFMA's opsel, which is four tiles only at BLOCK_M 256
+#: -- so a destination's row band is 256 rows here, not blockscale's 128, and M
+#: pads to a multiple of ``tp_size * 256``.
+_BLOCK_M = 256
+
+
+def _padded_m(m: int, world_size: int) -> int:
+    from mori.ops.gemm_ar import padded_m
+
+    return padded_m(m, world_size, _BLOCK_M)
+
+
+_logged_config = False
+
+
+def _shuffled_once():
+    global _logged_config
+    if _logged_config:
+        return True
+    _logged_config = True
+    return False
+
+
+def _fused_weight(layer):
+    """The op's B operand and B scale, or None if this layer cannot be fused."""
+    global _warned_layout
+    if not mxfp8_ready(layer):
+        if not _warned_layout:
+            _warned_layout = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "mori fused wo_b: neither gfx950 mxfp8 route prepared this "
+                "layer (weight shape %s), which the fused kernel requires; "
+                "not fusing.",
+                tuple(layer.weight.shape),
+            )
+        return None
+    return mori_weight(layer)
+
+
+class _FusedWoB:
+    """The TP communicator and mori's op, one per rank.
+
+    Holds the cco ``Communicator`` built from sglang's TP group, which is the
+    part mori cannot construct for us.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, m_max: int, n: int, k: int):
+        import torch.distributed as dist
+        from mori.cco import Communicator, UniqueId
+        from mori.ops.gemm_ar import GemmAllReduceOp
+        from sglang.srt.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+        tp = get_tp_group()
+        self.rank = tp.rank_in_group
+        self.world_size = tp.world_size
+        self.n, self.k, self.m_max = n, k, m_max
+
+        payload = [bytes(Communicator.get_unique_id()) if self.rank == 0 else None]
+        dist.broadcast_object_list(payload, src=tp.ranks[0], group=tp.cpu_group)
+        uid = UniqueId.from_bytes(payload[0])
+
+        # The window is VMM memory outside torch's allocator, so the run has to
+        # leave room for it (lower --mem-fraction-static). Sized from m_max, and
+        # it cannot grow afterwards.
+        gather_dtype = (
+            "fp8" if envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_FP8_GATHER.get() else "bf16"
+        )
+        window_bytes = GemmAllReduceOp.window_bytes_for(
+            self.world_size,
+            m_max=m_max,
+            n=n,
+            block_m=_BLOCK_M,
+            gather_dtype=gather_dtype,
+        )
+        self._comm_ctx = Communicator.init(
+            self.world_size,
+            self.rank,
+            uid,
+            per_rank_vmm=4 * window_bytes + (512 << 20),
+        )
+        self.comm = self._comm_ctx.__enter__()
+        try:
+            # Which way the fp8 gather moves. The LSA pull widens on the way in
+            # instead of in a second kernel, and it wins in both places: 951us
+            # against SDMA's 1011 on the layer, 1041.2ms of GPU busy against
+            # 1052.1 in the server.
+            self.op = GemmAllReduceOp(
+                self.comm,
+                n=n,
+                k=k,
+                m_max=m_max,
+                quant="mxfp8",
+                gather_dtype=gather_dtype,
+                gather_transport=os.environ.get(
+                    "SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_GATHER_TRANSPORT", "lsa"
+                ),
+            )
+            # Prove the collective moves bytes before serving a token. A mori
+            # built with BUILD_CCO_SDMA=OFF compiles the puts out: the kernels
+            # still launch, the all-reduce returns mostly the local slice, and
+            # the model answers fluently while being wrong -- and measures
+            # *faster*, having moved nothing.
+            self.op.self_test()
+        except Exception:
+            # The communicator holds a VMM reservation the whole process pays
+            # for. Half-constructing this object and leaving it open makes the
+            # *fallback* path fail too, which is how a simple attribute error
+            # here once took the server down.
+            self._comm_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
+            raise
+        logger.info(
+            "mori fused wo_b: window %.0f MiB, tp=%d, M<=%d, N=%d, K=%d, gather=%s",
+            self.op.window_bytes / 2**20,
+            self.world_size,
+            m_max,
+            n,
+            k,
+            gather_dtype,
+        )
+
+    def pad_rows(self, x: torch.Tensor, m_pad: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.op.pad_rows(x, m_pad)
+
+    def run(self, q_input, x_scale_raw, weight, weight_scale) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.op(q_input, weight, x_scale_raw, weight_scale)
+
+
+def _window_m_max(m_pad: int, world_size: int) -> int:
+    """Rows the symmetric window is sized for.
+
+    Taken from the chunked-prefill limit rather than the first request seen, so
+    a short prompt arriving first cannot fix a window too small for a full chunk
+    later -- the window cannot grow once allocated.
+    """
+    # `get_global_server_args()` is retired; the scheduling namespace carries
+    # the value in effect, which is what the other layers read.
+    from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_schedule
+
+    limit = get_schedule().chunked_prefill_size
+    if limit is not None and limit > 0:
+        return max(m_pad, _padded_m(limit, world_size))
+    return m_pad
+
+
+def _eligible(m: int, n: int, k: int, world_size: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether fusing is both expressible and worth it at this shape.
+
+    mori's ``supports`` answers the first; the thresholds here answer the
+    second, which is not a property of the kernel.
+    """
+    from mori.ops.gemm_ar import supports
+
+    if not supports(m, n, k, world_size, quant="mxfp8"):
+        return False
+    floor = (
+        _MIN_FUSED_M_FP8_GATHER
+        if envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR_FP8_GATHER.get()
+        else _MIN_FUSED_M
+    )
+    m_pad = _padded_m(m, world_size)
+    return m_pad >= floor and m >= _MIN_PAD_FILL * m_pad
+
+
+def _mori_has_gemm_ar() -> bool:
+    """Whether the pinned mori carries ``ops.gemm_ar``, memoised.
+
+    Checked rather than assumed because the import sits on the per-call path
+    below the switch: a mori predating the op would raise from inside a forward
+    rather than fall back.
+    """
+    global _mori_ok, _disabled
+    if _mori_ok is None:
+        try:
+            import mori.ops.gemm_ar  # noqa: F401
+
+            _mori_ok = True
+        except ImportError as err:
+            _mori_ok = False
+            _disabled = True
+            logger.warning(
+                "mori fused wo_b: this mori has no ops.gemm_ar, so the fused "
+                "path is off for this process: %s",
+                err,
+            )
+    return _mori_ok
+
+
+def fused_wo_b_available() -> bool:
+    """Static gate, cheap enough to call per layer."""
+    return (
+        not _disabled
+        and envs.SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_WO_B_AR.get()
+        and _mori_has_gemm_ar()
+    )
+
+
+def fused_wo_b(layer, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """wo_b's `GEMM + all-reduce`, fused. ``None`` means "use the normal path".
+
+    ``x`` is the bf16 activation this rank holds, ``[M, K]``. The result is the
+    all-reduced ``[M, N]``, as a **view of the symmetric window** -- the next
+    layer's wo_b overwrites it, which is safe because the caller consumes it in
+    the residual add of the same layer. ``SGLANG_DEBUG_FUSED_WO_B_AR`` forces a copy
+    and cross-checks against the unfused path.
+    """
+    global _state, _disabled
+
+    if not fused_wo_b_available():
+        return None
+
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.mxfp8_amd_gfx95 import Fp8GridActivation
+    from sglang.srt.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    # wo_a hands wo_b either a plain bf16 activation or an Fp8GridActivation --
+    # a bf16 tensor already rounded onto wo_b's fp8 grid, so quantising it below
+    # is lossless rather than a second rounding. Either way what the GEMM needs
+    # is the bf16 tensor.
+    if isinstance(x, Fp8GridActivation):
+        x = x.x
+    # wo_a's MXFP8 epilogue (SGLANG_HIP_WO_A_MXFP8) instead hands over fp8 plus
+    # a ue8m0 scale, with no bf16 left to quantise, and the op does its own
+    # quantisation. Only decode reaches that form, which _eligible declines on
+    # M anyway, so declining here costs no fusing.
+    if not isinstance(x, torch.Tensor):
+        return None
+
+    m, k = x.shape
+    if not hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_mx_e8m0"):
+        return None
+    n, w_k = mxfp8_shape(layer)
+    if w_k != k:
+        return None
+    world_size = get_tp_group().world_size
+    eligible = _eligible(m, n, k, world_size)
+    if _SHAPE_LOG:
+        _record_shape(m, eligible, world_size)
+    if not eligible:
+        return None
+
+    m_pad = _padded_m(m, world_size)
+    try:
+        if _state is None:
+            _state = _FusedWoB(
+                m_max=_window_m_max(m_pad, world_size),
+                n=n,
+                k=k,
+            )
+        if m_pad > _state.m_max or n != _state.n or k != _state.k:
+            return None
+        prepared = _fused_weight(layer)
+        if prepared is None:
+            return None
+        weight, b_scale = prepared
+        x_in = x if m_pad == m else _state.pad_rows(x, m_pad)
+        # The quantiser writes mori's packed scale layout itself, so there is no
+        # conversion pass after it. Zero-padded rows quantise to zero values
+        # (their scale is tiny but finite), and rows are independent in a GEMM,
+        # so the padding contributes nothing to any real row.
+        q_input, x_scale = quantize_packed(x_in)
+        out = _state.run(q_input, x_scale, weight, b_scale)
+        out = out[:m]
+    except ValueError as err:

nodes.body:
**An extra copy of every layer's `wo_b` weight, allocated after the KV cache is sized.**

`_mori_b` (the re-laid-out weight plus an int32 B scale) is built lazily on the first eligible call, i.e. while serving, after the memory profiler has already sized the KV cache. The original weight stays as well (the unfused path still needs it for decode), so this is a second copy of `wo_b` on each of the 61 layers. The env var's comment only asks users to lower `--mem-fraction-static` for the window.

Suggest building it at weight-processing time so the profiler accounts for it, or at least including it in the memory guidance. As it stands, a lazy OOM here lands in the rank-local `except Exception` path (see the comment there).

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Fused GEMM + all-reduce for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ``wo_b`` on ROCm gfx950, via mori cco.
+
+``wo_b`` is a ``RowParallelLinear``: an mxfp8 GEMM and then an all-reduce of the
+``[M, hidden]`` result. mori's fused kernel writes each destination's row band
+into a symmetric window and hands it to the SDMA copy engines as soon as that
+band's tiles are done, so the transfer runs inside the GEMM; the reduce and
+all-gather still run as their own kernels.
+
+A mori built with ``BUILD_CCO_SDMA=OFF`` compiles the puts out, and then the
+all-reduce returns mostly the local slice while the model still answers -- and
+measures *faster*, having moved no bytes. ``GemmAllReduceOp.self_test()`` is
+what catches that; the flag has been ON by default since ROCm/mori#710.
+
+Needs ``MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=1`` at process start and a layer one of the two gfx950
+mxfp8 routes prepared -- see ``mxfp8_route``.
+
+The fused epilogue pushes a whole ``BLOCK_M`` row band to one destination, so M
+must be a multiple of ``tp_size * 256``. That granule is mxfp8's, not a choice
+-- see ``_BLOCK_M``. Ragged M is zero-padded up to it, which costs GEMM rows and
+buys the overlap -- see ``_MIN_PAD_FILL``. Decode and small batches fall back to
+the ordinary path, and that is expected rather than a failure.
+
+``mori.ops.gemm_ar.GemmAllReduceOp`` owns the symmetric window, the per-M
+compile cache and the row padding. What stays here is sglang's: the TP
+communicator, how the window is sized, the operand conversions, and whether
+fusing is worth it at this shape.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import os
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# ---- operand conversion ----------------------------------------------
+
+#: Rows one packed A-scale group spans, and the rows one quantiser program owns.
+#: They are the same 64 by construction, which is what lets the quantiser write
+#: mori's layout without any extra traffic -- see `_mxfp8_quant_packed_kernel`.
+QUANT_BLOCK_M = 64
+
+
+def mxfp8_shape(layer) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """The layer's logical ``(N, K)``, read off the ue8m0 scale.
+
+    **Not** ``layer.weight.shape``: the native route rebinds the weight to its
+    shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, and reading that first axis as N
+    disqualifies every layer without a word.
+    """
+    sn, sk = layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0.shape
+    return sn * 32, sk * 32
+
+
+def mxfp8_route(layer) -> str | None:
+    """Which gfx950 mxfp8 route prepared this layer, or None if neither did.
+
+    Both leave the ``[N/32, K/32]`` exponent bytes on
+    ``layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0`` and differ only in the weight: ``native``
+    rebinds it to the shuffled ``[N/16, K/128, 2048]``, ``aiter`` leaves plain
+    ``[N, K]``. Reading one as the other returns an uncorrelated result rather
+    than failing, so `mori_weight` branches on this instead of guessing.
+    """
+    if not hasattr(layer, "weight_scale_mx_e8m0"):
+        return None
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_native_ready", False):
+        return "native"
+    if getattr(layer, "mxfp8_aiter_ready", False):
+        return "aiter"
+    return None
+
+
+def mxfp8_ready(layer) -> bool:
+    """Whether either gfx950 mxfp8 route already prepared this layer."""
+    return mxfp8_route(layer) is not None
+
+
+def mori_weight(layer):
+    """The layer's B operand and B scale in mori's layouts, cached on the layer.
+
+    sglang and mori differ only in how a lane's two 64-wide K sub-blocks sit:
+    sglang interleaves them inside its 32 bytes, mori keeps them as two 16-byte
+    blocks. Cached because the permutation copies the whole weight.
+    """
+    cached = getattr(layer, "_mori_b", None)
+    if cached is not None:
+        return cached
+    n, k = mxfp8_shape(layer)
+    w = layer.weight.data.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    if mxfp8_route(layer) == "aiter":
+        # That route leaves the weight in its checkpoint [N, K] order, which is
+        # what preshuffle_b is defined on, so mori emits its own layout from the
+        # source rather than permuting sglang's.
+        from mori.ops.gemm_ar import preshuffle_b
+
+        b = preshuffle_b(w.reshape(n, k).view(layer.weight.dtype))
+    else:
+        # [N/16, K/128, 64 lanes, 2 sub-blocks, 16B] -> the two sub-blocks split out
+        b = (
+            w.reshape(n // 16, k // 128, 64, 2, 16)
+            .permute(0, 1, 3, 2, 4)
+            .contiguous()
+            .reshape(n, k)
+            .view(layer.weight.dtype)
+        )
+    b_scale = (
+        layer.weight_scale_mx_e8m0.data.contiguous()
+        .view(torch.uint8)
+        .t()
+        .contiguous()
+        .to(torch.int32)
+        .reshape(-1)
+    )
+    layer._mori_b = (b, b_scale)

nodes.body:
**Without chunked prefill the window is still sized by the first request.**

When `chunked_prefill_size` is `None` / `-1`, `m_max` falls back to the first eligible `m_pad`, which is the first-request sizing the docstring says this avoids (mori's `GemmAllReduceOp` docstring also says to size `m_max` for the largest M the deployment will see). Every later, larger M then hits `m_pad > _state.m_max` (line 488) and silently returns `None` for the rest of the process.

Suggest sizing from an explicit upper bound in that case (e.g. `max_prefill_tokens`), and logging once when a call is declined for exceeding `m_max`.
